exercise.name: Dumbbell Incline One Arm Hammer Press

reference.title: Dumbbell Incline One Arm Hammer Press
reference.listing: Page could not be read (blocked by the network proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you lower the dumbbell, exhale as you press it up.
breathing.cadence: About 2.0 s down, 0.3 s pause, 1.2 s up

prescription.tempo: 2-0-1-0 (2 s down, no pause, 1 s up)
prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9).
prescription.progression: Add reps up to the top of the range, then the next dumbbell; finish all reps on the weaker arm first.

cues.text: Back pad at 30 degrees, glutes in the crease, upper back and head on the pad, feet planted wide; one dumbbell over the right shoulder with the palm facing in, the free hand on the stomach.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell beside the upper chest, elbow tucked about 30 degrees from the side, forearm vertical.
Handle beside the upper chest, palm still facing in; brief pause.
Breathe out and press straight up until the arm is straight over the shoulder.
Pause at the top, chest square, then lower again. Switch arms after the set.

mistakes.mistake: Trunk rolling toward the working arm
mistakes.fix: Brace the trunk and plant the opposite foot; both shoulder blades stay on the pad.
Keep the elbow close to the ribs with the palm facing in.

mistakes.mistake: Dumbbell tipping as the wrist turns
mistakes.fix: Keep the handle along the body and the wrist straight.

mistakes.mistake: Bouncing out of the bottom or cutting the range short
mistakes.fix: Lower under control to beside the chest, pause, then press.
Keep the glutes down and both feet planted.

kinematics.norm: Arm straight but not locked at the top; about 90-110 degrees at the bottom (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Elbow flare (upper arm from the trunk)
kinematics.norm: About 20-40 degrees from the body at the bottom with the neutral grip (clinical opinion)
Up from beside the chest to over the shoulder (clinical opinion)
Free hand resting on the stomach (clinical opinion)
Feet flat, knees about 80-90 degrees (clinical opinion)
About 2 s down, a short pause, 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

cautions: Get into position safely: sit with the dumbbells on the thighs, lie back and kick them up with the knees; at the end of the set bring them back to the thighs rather than dropping them (clinical opinion).
Shoulder pain: shorten the range at the bottom until it settles (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrists straight over the forearms; bent-back wrists under a heavy dumbbell strain the wrist.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Lower back arching: feet on a low step.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main pusher with a shift toward the upper fibres on a 30-degree incline (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020; Lauver 2016).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Works harder as the bench rises (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the shoulder blade against the rib cage while the arm presses.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Works as a stabiliser; biceps activity rose with the stability demand, highest with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blade drawn back on the bench.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the trunk square while only one side is loaded; unilateral pressing raised trunk muscle activity (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the trunk being pulled toward the loaded side.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the trunk being pulled toward the loaded side.
